decisive_items: FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene positive on RT-PCR
response.rationale: C1 is the only candidate that names the fusion-gene-defined subtype and is anchored to the pathognomonic RT-PCR result. R6 correctly identifies CEL from marrow hypercellularity/eosinophilia but omits the FIP1L1-PDGFRA etiology; R2/R3 are too broad, R5/R4 overread the dermal histiocytic infiltrate as primary, and R1 uses tryptase alone without mast-cell evidence.

rejected.why: Only skin lesions plus eosinophilia; lacks marrow and fusion-gene evidence.
Elevated tryptase is nonspecific and not backed by mast-cell infiltrate; FIP1L1-PDGFRA is decisive.
Histiocytic/IHC findings are a secondary tissue reaction; CD1a negativity and fusion gene favor CEL subtype.
Fusion-positive eosinophilia is classified as CEL/myeloid neoplasm, not generic HES.
Overly broad eosinophilic disorder label; misses the pathognomonic fusion gene.
